elements.label: Figure O.19
elements.description: Waterfall chart titled "Impact of fiscal policy on inequality, 2018". Y-axis: "Percentage Point Reduction", scale 0 to 6.0 in steps of 1.0. X-axis categories, left to right: Cash transfers, PIT, Other direct taxes, SSC/HI, Disposable income, Electricity subsidy, VAT, Excises, Environmental tax, Consumable income, Education, Health, Final income. No values are printed on the bars; approximate readings are: Cash transfers ~0.5 (bar from 0 to ~0.5); PIT ~0.5 to ~1.0; Other direct taxes ~1.0 to ~1.2; SSC/HI ~1.2 to ~2.7; Disposable income total ~2.7; Electricity subsidy ~2.7 to ~2.9; VAT ~2.7 to ~2.8; Excises ~2.7 to ~2.8; Environmental tax ~2.7 (near zero increment); Consumable income total ~2.7; Education ~2.7 to ~4.4; Health ~4.4 to ~4.9; Final income total ~4.9. Bars are colored by type (blue for direct taxes and transfers, green for indirect transfers and taxes, orange for in-kind, and totals in darker shades). The pattern is a cumulative build-up from about 0 to about 4.9 points, with the largest single increments coming from SSC/HI and Education. A note reads: "The blue bars are direct taxes and transfers. The green bars are indirect transfers and taxes. The orange bars are in-kind. Poverty is measured at the $3.20 per person per day in 2011PPP terms used for LMICs."

elements.description: Vertical bar chart titled "Reduction in inequality due to fiscal policy in international context". Y-axis: "Point change in the Gini Index", scale 0 to -25 in steps of 5. Countries are grouped by income level: High income (teal), Upper middle income (orange), Lower middle income (teal, with Vietnam highlighted in purple), and Lower income (orange). Approximate readings, with no values printed: High income: Poland ~-11.5, Croatia ~-9.5, Panama ~-8.4, Uruguay ~-8.1, Chile ~-6.8, Romania ~-6.5. Upper middle income: Namibia ~-20.1, Argentina ~-17.0, South Africa ~-17.0, Costa Rica ~-10.0, Brazil ~-8.8, Mexico ~-8.1, Iran ~-7.9, Mexico ~-7.8, Mexico ~-7.5, Ecuador ~-6.8, Belarus ~-5.9, Colombia ~-5.9, Colombia ~-5.5, Venezuela ~-5.2, Russia ~-5.1, Albania ~-4.7, Dominican Republic ~-4.6, Paraguay ~-4.2, Armenia ~-4.0, Peru ~-3.7, Peru ~-3.3, Indonesia ~-2.2, Guatemala ~-1.8, Jordan ~-1.7. Lower middle income: Ukraine ~-8.2, Tunisia ~-7.3, Kenya ~-5.9, El Salvador ~-5.1, Bolivia ~-5.1, Vietnam ~-4.6 (highlighted), Tanzania ~-4.3, Nicaragua ~-4.0, Egypt ~-3.8, Ghana ~-2.9, Comoros ~-2.8, Honduras ~-2.0, Sri Lanka ~-1.5. Lower income: Burkina Faso ~-3.0, Uganda ~-2.7, Ethiopia ~-1.7. The pattern is that most countries show Gini reductions between about -2 and -10, with Namibia, Argentina and South Africa the largest outliers at about -17 to -20, and Vietnam sits in the lower-middle range. A note reads: "Pensions treated as deferred income." Source: CEQ and World Bank databases and World Bank calculations (see Rodriguez and Wai-Poi, 2020).
